hook: Aggressive blood pressure control in diabetes did not cut dementia risk, but slowed brain lesion growth.

readout.label: Hazard ratio, dementia or MCI, intensive arm

summary: In a randomized trial of 12,434 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, targeting systolic pressure below 120 instead of 140 mm Hg did not significantly change dementia or mild cognitive impairment over a median of 3.8 years. In an MRI subset of 862 people, intensive treatment led to a smaller increase in white matter lesions. The trial was open label, and the MRI result comes from a small subset.
title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
